messages:
julia.ops: FYI rolling a driver + CUDA + NCCL bump tomorrow 03:00 UTC to enable newer SM90 kernels on H100 fleet. Target: NVIDIA driver 535.86, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.15. Will canary on 4 nodes in eu-west-2 then expand. :rocket:

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance window created for 1765219200 (tomorrow 03:00 UTC) — canary pool: h100-canary-4

teo.eng: started canary, one node is failing to bring up runtime: containers crash during model warmup with a JIT error.

teo.eng: paste of the error from runtime logs:
```
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
ptxas info   : Compiling entry function 'kernel_main'
ptxas info   : Function properties for kernel_main
jit: unsupported PTX version '90' (compiled for sm_90?)
libcuda: cuModuleLoadData failed: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE
```

maria.ml: interesting — this only shows up on instances launched from the older eu-west-2 AMI build (ami-h100-2024-11). Newer AMI in us-west-2 looks fine. Could be a kernel/toolchain mismatch on the host (glibc / gcc used for driver modules).

sanjay.infra: confirms: failing hosts are all H100 (SM90) in eu-west-2 and a single us-west-2 canary. SM80/SM86 nodes unaffected. Suspect driver minimum mismatch: compiled PTX for sm_90 requires a newer runtime driver.

teo.eng: quick repro script attached to thread (ran on failing node): `python tools/repro_ptx.py --model gptx --device 0` — it fails immediately with the same ptxAS error.

sanjay.infra: short mitigation while we triage: set NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 for the pod and force runtime to use precompiled cubin if available. Also pause rollout and rollback driver on the canary that failed to the previous stable 525.x image.
maria.ml: can we avoid broad rollback? capacity in eu-west-2 is tight this week — rolling back all H100s will bump cost (use of reserved capacity) and block other jobs. Maybe do targeted rollback only on the 2 failing hosts and mark them DRAIN:NETWORK to stop scheduling.
sanjay.infra: agreed, do targeted rollback + drain. I'll also flip kernel module autoload to enforce the older driver until we have a fix.

nvidia-rep: thanks for the heads up — please include full dmesg + `nvidia-smi -q` output and the output of `cuobjdump --dump-ptx` for the failing module; we'll open an internal bug tracker entry. We've seen PTX/SM90 JIT issues when the driver ABI is older than the PTX target.

teo.eng: grabbing logs now, posting snippets here. dmesg shows "nvidia: module taints kernel — version mismatch" and `nvidia-smi` reports driver 535.86 on the nodes that failed but the modules loaded are from 525.105 — weird mix.

maria.ml: that points to AMI bake problem: kernel module packaging step didn't replace the DKMS-built modules; AMI still carrying old modules, driver package claims new version but modules are old -> JIT can't link.

sanjay.infra: next steps I'm going to take now:
- rollback driver package on the two failed canaries to stable 525.x (sanjay.infra)
- drain failed hosts from scheduler (sanjay.infra)
- pause the global rollout (julia.ops)
- collect full artifacts and open NV support ticket (julia.ops)
- teo to run repro on the drained hosts and capture cuobjdump/cubin + strace (teo.eng)

julia.ops: pausing the rollout now. Not expanding beyond canary pool. Will update incident in #incidents and notify SRE oncall.

deploy-bot: incident created: #incidents/1765123456-ptx-runtime-compat.

teo.eng: quick workaround verified: forcing runtime to load precompiled cubins (KERNEL_PRECOMPILE=1) lets the container start, but performance drops ~15% and some ops still fallback. We can use that as short-term mitigation for critical customer jobs.
maria.ml: note for product: if we postpone the upgrade, customers using H100 may continue to miss micro-optimizations we shipped in the new runtime. Need trade-off doc on cost vs quality.
sanjay.infra: open questions: why did AMI pipeline not replace DKMS modules? I'll audit the bake logs and get back. Also need to check if our canary gating tested module load + cuobjdump verification.
nvidia-rep: NV support ticket opened (case 1234567) with requested artifacts. We'll escalate with driver engineers for PTX mismatch.

julia.ops: summary / action owners: rollback two canaries (sanjay.infra), collect traces + cuobjdump (teo.eng), pause rollout + open ticket (julia.ops), communicate to customer-facing teams (maria.ml).

teo.eng: ack. Starting repro collection now. ETA 30min. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sanjay.infra: I'll post the bake audit trail in an hour. If no blocker found, we'll re-run AMI bake with explicit DKMS rebuild step.

maria.ml: tagging @customer-success to prep comms if any paid customers notice perf regressions.

julia.ops: thanks all — keep thread updated. We'll reconvene after NV reply or when repro artifacts are ready. :white_check_mark:
